subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Complete A/L Biology curriculum covering cell biology, molecular biology, genetics, ecology, and more.
subjects.descriptionSi: කෝෂ ජීව විද්‍යාව, අණුක ජීව විද්‍යාව, ජාන විද්‍යාව, පරිසර විද්‍යාව සහ තවත් බොහෝ දේ ආවරණය කරන සම්පූර්ණ A/L ජීව විද්‍යා පාඨ්‍යක්‍රමය.

units.title: Cell Biology
units.description: Explore the fundamental unit of life — cells. Learn about their structure, organelles, and how they divide.
units.descriptionSi: ජීවයේ මූලික ඒකකය — සෛල ගැන ඉගෙන ගන්න. ඒවායේ ව්‍යුහය, අංග සහ ඒවා බෙදෙන ආකාරය ඉගෙන ගන්න.

units.title: Molecular Biology
units.description: Dive into the molecular mechanisms of life — DNA structure, replication, and protein synthesis.
units.descriptionSi: ජීවයේ අණුක යාන්ත්‍රණයන් ගැන ගැඹුරට යන්න — DNA ව්‍යුහය, ප්‍රතිපාතනය සහ ප්‍රෝටීන සංශ්ලේෂණය.

units.title: Ecology
units.description: Understand how organisms interact with each other and their environment — from food chains to biodiversity.
units.descriptionSi: ආහාර දාම සිට ජෛව විවිධත්වය දක්වා — ක්ෂුද්‍ර ජීවීන් එකිනෙකා සහ ඔවුන්ගේ පරිසරය සමඟ අන්තර්ක්‍රියා කරන ආකාරය තේරුම් ගන්න.

topics.title: Cell Structure
topics.description: Understand the components of plant and animal cells including organelles, membranes, and cytoplasm.
topics.descriptionSi: ශාක සහ සතුන්ගේ සෛලවල සංඝටක ඇතුළත් අංග, ඝනපට, සහ සයිටෝප්ලාස්මය තේරුම් ගන්න.

topics.title: DNA Structure
topics.description: Learn about the double helix model of DNA, base pairing rules, and the process of DNA replication.
topics.descriptionSi: DNA හි ද්විත්ව හෙලික්ස් ආකෘතිය, මූල සම්බන්ධතා නීති සහ DNA ප්‍රතිපාතන ක්‍රියාවලිය ගැන ඉගෙන ගන්න.

topics.title: Ecosystems
topics.description: Explore how energy flows through ecosystems via food chains and food webs.
topics.descriptionSi: ආහාර දාම සහ ආහාර ජාල හරහා පරිසර පද්ධති හරහා ශක්තිය ගලා යන ආකාරය ගවේෂණය කරන්න.

topics.title: Cell Division
topics.description: Study the processes of mitosis and meiosis — how cells replicate and produce gametes.
topics.descriptionSi: මයිටෝසිස් සහ මයෝසිස් ක්‍රියාවලි අධ්‍යයනය — සෛල ප්‍රතිපාතනය සහ ගැමීට නිෂ්පාදනය කරන ආකාරය.

topics.title: Protein Synthesis
topics.description: The central dogma of molecular biology — transcription of DNA to mRNA and translation at ribosomes.
topics.descriptionSi: අණුක ජීව විද්‍යාවේ මධ්‍ය මතය — DNA සිට mRNA ට පරිවර්තනය සහ රයිබොසෝමවල පරිවර්තනය.

topics.title: Biodiversity
topics.description: The variety of life on Earth — species diversity, genetic diversity, and ecosystem diversity.
topics.descriptionSi: පෘථිවියේ ජීවයේ විවිධත්වය — විශේෂ විවිධත්වය, ජාන විවිධත්වය සහ පරිසර පද්ධති විවිධත්වය.

subtopics.title: Plant Cell
subtopics.description: Structure and organelles unique to plant cells including the cell wall, chloroplasts, and large central vacuole.
subtopics.descriptionSi: සෛල බිත්තිය, හරිතලවක සහ විශාල මධ්‍ය හිස් කුටීරය ඇතුළත් ශාක සෛලවලට ආවේණික ව්‍යුහය සහ අංග.
subtopics.content: Plant cells are eukaryotic cells that have a rigid cell wall, chloroplasts for photosynthesis, and a large central vacuole for storage and maintaining turgor pressure. Key organelles include the nucleus, mitochondria, endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi apparatus, ribosomes, and lysosomes.

subtopics.title: DNA Double Helix
subtopics.description: Watson and Crick's model of DNA — the antiparallel sugar-phosphate backbone, nitrogenous base pairing, and hydrogen bonds.
subtopics.descriptionSi: DNA හි වොට්සන් සහ ක්‍රික් ආකෘතිය — ප්‍රතිවිරුද්ධ සීනි-ෆොස්ෆේට් කොඳු ඇටය, නයිට්‍රජනීය මූල සම්බන්ධතා, සහ ස්ථානික සබඳතා.
subtopics.content: DNA is a double-stranded helical molecule composed of nucleotides. Each nucleotide contains a deoxyribose sugar, a phosphate group, and one of four nitrogenous bases: adenine (A), thymine (T), guanine (G), or cytosine (C). The two strands run antiparallel and are held together by hydrogen bonds between complementary base pairs (A-T and G-C).

subtopics.title: Mitosis
subtopics.description: The process of nuclear division producing two genetically identical daughter cells — prophase, metaphase, anaphase, and telophase.
subtopics.descriptionSi: ස්ථානික වශයෙන් සමාන දේහපාලි සෛල දෙකක් නිපදවන න්‍යෂ්ටි බෙදීමේ ක්‍රියාවලිය — ප්‍රෝෆේස්, මෙටාෆේස්, අනාෆේස් සහ ටෙලෝෆේස්.
subtopics.content: Mitosis is a type of cell division that results in two daughter cells each having the same number and kind of chromosomes as the parent nucleus. It is essential for growth, repair, and asexual reproduction. The phases are prophase, prometaphase, metaphase, anaphase, and telophase, followed by cytokinesis.

subtopics.title: Transcription
subtopics.description: RNA polymerase binding, initiation, elongation, and termination — producing mRNA from a DNA template.
subtopics.descriptionSi: RNA පොලිමරේස් බැඳීම, ආරම්භය, දිගු කිරීම සහ අවසන් කිරීම — DNA මූලාවරණයෙන් mRNA නිෂ්පාදනය.
subtopics.content: Transcription is the process of copying a segment of DNA into mRNA. RNA polymerase binds to the promoter region, unwinds the DNA, and synthesizes a complementary RNA strand in the 5' to 3' direction. The process has three stages: initiation, elongation, and termination. In eukaryotes, the pre-mRNA undergoes processing including 5' capping, 3' polyadenylation, and splicing to remove introns.

subtopics.title: Food Chains
subtopics.description: Linear sequences of organisms showing energy transfer from producers to consumers to decomposers.
subtopics.descriptionSi: උත්පාදකයන්ගෙන් පරිභෝජකයන්ට සහ වික්ෂෝපකයන්ට ශක්ති හුවමාරුව පෙන්වන ක්ෂුද්‍ර ජීවීන්ගේ සෘජු අනුපිළිවෙල.
subtopics.content: A food chain is a linear sequence of organisms through which nutrients and energy pass as one organism eats another. It starts with producers (plants), followed by primary consumers (herbivores), secondary consumers (carnivores), and tertiary consumers. Decomposers break down dead organic matter, returning nutrients to the soil.

subtopics.title: Translation
subtopics.description: mRNA decoding at the ribosome — codons, tRNA, amino acids, and polypeptide chain assembly.
subtopics.descriptionSi: රයිබොසෝමයේ mRNA විකේතනය — කෝඩෝන, tRNA, ඇමයිනෝ අම්ල සහ පොලිපෙප්ටයිඩ් දාම සංයෝජනය.
subtopics.content: Translation occurs at ribosomes where mRNA is decoded to synthesize polypeptide chains. Transfer RNA (tRNA) molecules carry specific amino acids to the ribosome, matching their anticodons with mRNA codons. The process involves initiation (small ribosomal subunit binding), elongation (peptide bond formation and translocation), and termination (release factor binding at stop codons). The resulting polypeptide folds into a functional protein.

subtopics.title: Energy Flow
subtopics.description: The 10% rule, trophic levels, and how energy is lost as heat at each level of the food chain.
subtopics.descriptionSi: 10% නීතිය, පෝෂණ මට්ටම් සහ ආහාර දාමයේ සෑම මට්ටමකම ශක්තිය තාපය ලෙස අහිමි වන ආකාරය.
subtopics.content: Energy flows through ecosystems in one direction, from the sun to producers and then through consumers. At each trophic level, approximately 90% of energy is lost as heat through cellular respiration. This is why food chains rarely have more than 4-5 trophic levels. An energy pyramid visually represents the decrease in available energy at each successive level.

subtopics.title: Animal Cell
subtopics.description: Structure and organelles of animal cells including the nucleus, mitochondria, and centrioles.
subtopics.descriptionSi: න්‍යෂ්ටිය, මයිටොකොන්ඩ්‍රියා සහ සෙන්ට්‍රියෝල ඇතුළත් සතුන්ගේ සෛලවල ව්‍යුහය සහ අංග.
subtopics.content: Animal cells are eukaryotic cells that lack a cell wall but contain centrioles for cell division. They have lysosomes for intracellular digestion, a cytoskeleton for structural support, and smaller vacuoles compared to plant cells. The cell membrane is the outermost layer.

subtopics.title: Meiosis
subtopics.description: Reduction division producing four haploid gametes — meiosis I and meiosis II, crossing over, and genetic variation.
subtopics.descriptionSi: හප්ලොයිඩ් ගැමීට සියල්ලන්ගෙන් ස්ථානික ලෙස නිපදවන අඩුකිරීමේ බෙදීම — මයෝසිස් I සහ මයෝසිස් II, හරහා යාම, සහ ජාන විවිධත්වය.
subtopics.content: Meiosis is a special type of cell division that reduces the chromosome number by half, producing four haploid cells. It occurs in two stages: meiosis I (separation of homologous chromosomes) and meiosis II (separation of sister chromatids). Crossing over during prophase I introduces genetic variation.

subtopics.title: DNA Replication
subtopics.description: Semi-conservative replication — unwinding, primer binding, elongation, and proofreading.
subtopics.descriptionSi: අර්ධ-සංරක්ෂිත ප්‍රතිපාතනය — විසුරුම, ප්‍රයෝමක බැඳීම, දිගු කිරීම සහ පරීක්ෂා කිරීම.
subtopics.content: DNA replication is semi-conservative, meaning each new DNA molecule consists of one old strand and one new strand. The process involves helicase unwinding the double helix, primase laying RNA primers, DNA polymerase III adding nucleotides in the 5' to 3' direction, and DNA ligase joining Okazaki fragments on the lagging strand. DNA polymerase I replaces RNA primers with DNA, and proofreading mechanisms ensure accuracy.

questions.stem: Which stage of mitosis is characterized by chromosomes aligning at the metaphase plate?
questions.explanation: During metaphase, chromosomes align along the metaphase plate (equator) of the cell before being pulled apart in anaphase.

questions.stem: How many daughter cells are produced by a single mitotic division, and what is their chromosome number relative to the parent?
questions.explanation: Mitosis produces two genetically identical diploid daughter cells, each with the same chromosome number as the parent cell.

options.text: 2 cells, the same number of chromosomes
4 cells, the same number of chromosomes

questions.stem: During which phase of meiosis does crossing over occur?
questions.explanation: Crossing over (exchange of genetic material between homologous chromosomes) occurs during prophase I of meiosis, contributing to genetic variation.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes mitosis from meiosis?
questions.explanation: Mitosis produces two identical diploid cells for growth and repair, whereas meiosis produces four genetically distinct haploid gametes.

options.text: Mitosis produces gametes, meiosis produces body cells
Meiosis halves the chromosome number; mitosis maintains it
Crossing over only happens in mitosis

questions.stem: Which organelle is the site of photosynthesis in plant cells?
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and carry out photosynthesis, converting light energy into chemical energy.

questions.stem: A structure present in animal cells but absent in plant cells is:
questions.explanation: Centrioles are found in animal cells and are involved in spindle formation during cell division; they are generally absent in higher plant cells.

questions.stem: What is the complementary base pair of adenine (A) in DNA?
questions.explanation: In DNA, adenine (A) always pairs with thymine (T) via two hydrogen bonds, while guanine (G) pairs with cytosine (C).

questions.stem: Which enzyme is responsible for unzipping the DNA double helix during replication?
questions.explanation: Helicase unwinds and separates the two DNA strands by breaking the hydrogen bonds between base pairs.

questions.stem: Which molecule carries amino acids to the ribosome during translation?
questions.explanation: Transfer RNA (tRNA) carries specific amino acids to the ribosome, matching its anticodon with the mRNA codon.

questions.stem: RNA processing in eukaryotes removes which regions of the pre-mRNA?
questions.explanation: During RNA processing, introns (non-coding regions) are removed by splicing, and exons (coding regions) are joined together.

questions.stem: What percentage of energy typically transfers from one trophic level to the next?
questions.explanation: Approximately 10% of energy is transferred between trophic levels; the rest is lost as heat through respiration.

questions.stem: In a food chain, which organisms form the first trophic level?
questions.explanation: Producers (autotrophs such as plants) form the first trophic level, capturing energy from the sun via photosynthesis.

questions.stem: Which type of biodiversity describes the variety of genes within a species?
questions.explanation: Genetic diversity refers to the variety of genes and alleles within a species, which increases its resilience and adaptability.
